articles.title: Thank You to Our 2026 Sponsors
articles.summary: Sutton Cricket Club thanks every business and individual who supported the club during the 2026 season.
articles.lead: Sutton Cricket Club would like to say a huge thank you to every sponsor who supported the club throughout the 2026 season.
body: The backing of local businesses and individuals makes a real difference to Sutton Cricket Club, helping us support senior cricket, junior development, women’s cricket, facilities, equipment and the wider running of the club.
Our 2026 supporters included Cheffins, AC Timbers, Polly Glaze, FTR Suspension, Latta Hire, Ports Plumbing and The Chequers, all of whom backed the club through pitchside and club sponsorship.
We were also grateful for match-ball support from Rimbles, East Skips and AMK Car Detailing.
David Frear continued his support of our junior cricket, while Envy Hair Salon supported the senior sides.
Every contribution, whether through sponsorship, match-ball support, team backing or other help, plays a part in keeping cricket thriving at Sutton.
Sponsorship allows us to keep investing in the club and creating opportunities for players of all ages, from our youngest juniors through to senior and women’s cricket.
We are hugely grateful to all of our 2026 sponsors for their continued support and for being part of the Sutton Cricket Club community.
Thank you for backing Sutton CC throughout the 2026 season. 🏏💛💚

articles.title: 2026 Saturday Season in Numbers
articles.summary: The key numbers from Sutton CC’s 2026 Saturday League season across the 1st XI and 2nd XI.
articles.lead: From hundreds and five-wicket hauls to leading run-scorers and wicket-takers, here are some of the standout numbers from Sutton Cricket Club’s 2026 Saturday League season.
body: Paul Robinson finished as Sutton’s leading Saturday league run-scorer across the two senior sides with 317 runs in total – 263 for the 2nd XI and a further 54 for the 1st XI.
Michael Grady scored 264 1st XI league runs at an average of 33.00, including a superb unbeaten 127.
James Nuttall made a huge impact in only six league innings, scoring 184 runs at 30.67 with a highest score of 136 and a strike rate of 141.54.
James Phipps scored 218 combined league runs across the two Saturday sides, including two half-centuries for the 2nd XI.
Craig Faux added 190 1st XI league runs, while James Barrett contributed 156 runs with a highest score of 65.
One of the biggest batting highlights of the season was the 241-run partnership between Michael Grady and James Nuttall against Bluntisham on 8 August.
Josh Grady finished as Sutton’s leading Saturday league wicket-taker with 22 wickets across the 1st XI and 2nd XI.
Michael Grady took 19 1st XI league wickets at an outstanding average of 9.47, including best figures of 5/24.
Jack Boston and Craig Faux both finished with 16 1st XI league wickets. Jack’s best return was 4/9, while Craig’s best was 4/22.
Michael Ward was one of the standout 2nd XI bowlers, taking 13 wickets at an average of just 9.15, including a five-wicket haul of 5/15.
George Ware took 12 Saturday league wickets across the two sides, including 10 for the 2nd XI at an economy rate of 3.71.
Richard Goodjohn produced one of the strongest short-run bowling returns of the season, taking nine 1st XI wickets at 11.56, including 5/17.
Cornelio Du Plessis also enjoyed an excellent 2nd XI bowling season, taking nine wickets at 11.44.
Jordan Emms combined eight wickets with an exceptional 2nd XI economy rate of 2.91.
With the gloves, Daniel Abbs recorded five 1st XI wicketkeeping dismissals, while Joshie Pollard recorded four across the two Saturday sides.

The numbers underline the depth of contribution across both Sutton Saturday teams, with match-winning performances coming from experienced players, all-rounders and emerging cricketers throughout the summer.

articles.title: Sutton CC 2026 Season Review
articles.summary: A look back at the 2026 season across Sutton Cricket Club, from senior and women’s cricket to juniors, awards and standout performances.
articles.lead: The 2026 season was another busy and memorable year for Sutton Cricket Club, with strong performances across the senior sides, continued growth in women’s and junior cricket, and plenty of individual highlights along the way.
body: The Saturday season saw Sutton’s 1st XI and 2nd XI compete throughout the summer, with several standout individual performances and plenty of contributions across both teams.

Michael Grady produced one of the performances of the season with an unbeaten 127 against Bluntisham, while James Nuttall also made a major impact with a superb 136 during the campaign. Their 241-run partnership was one of the biggest batting highlights of the year.

With the ball, Josh Grady led Sutton’s Saturday league wicket-taking with 22 wickets across the two sides. Michael Grady took 19 1st XI league wickets at an average of 9.47, while Jack Boston and Craig Faux both finished with 16 1st XI league wickets.
The 2nd XI also produced some excellent bowling performances, including Michael Ward’s 13 wickets at an average of 9.15 and George Ware’s 10 wickets at an economy rate of 3.71.

Paul Robinson was one of the most consistent Saturday batters of the season, scoring 263 league runs for the 2nd XI at 43.83 and adding a further 54 for the 1st XI. James Phipps also contributed strongly across both Saturday sides.

Away from the Saturday teams, the Sunday and Development side continued to provide important opportunities for players to gain match experience and for younger cricketers to make the step towards senior cricket.
Women’s cricket continued to grow at Sutton & Haddenham during 2026, with both softball and hardball opportunities giving more players the chance to represent the club and develop their game.

The women’s end-of-season awards recognised another strong year, with Izzy Biswell named Hardball Player, Mia Karpinaite Softball Player, Lucy Marsh receiving the Team Spirit award, Georgina Lister named Coaches’ Player, Charlotte Hough Players’ Player and Karen Thorpe receiving the Jon Megginson Memorial award.

Junior cricket remained at the heart of the club. All Stars, U12 Softball and U14 cricket provided regular opportunities for young players throughout the summer, supported by coaches, scorers, parents and volunteers.

The season also brought success and recognition at the club’s annual awards. Michael Grady was named 1st XI Batter of the Year and Player of the Year, with Josh Grady taking the 1st XI Bowler award. James Short was 2nd XI Batter of the Year, Michael Ward 2nd XI Bowler of the Year and Paul Robinson 2nd XI Player of the Year.

Kaiden Grady was named Sunday Player of the Year, Vini Vineeth Fielder of the Year, George Ware Clubman and Josh Pollard Young Player of the Year. The U14 awards went to Leon Perrin as Batter of the Year, Jason Harnwell as Bowler of the Year and Oscar Pergl-Wilson as Player of the Year.

One of the most important events away from league cricket was the Colin Coulson Memorial Game, which brought players, families and supporters together and raised £275 for the British Heart Foundation.
The club also continued to benefit from the support of sponsors, volunteers, coaches, scorers, ground staff, parents and supporters, all of whom played a part in making the 2026 season possible.

As Sutton Cricket Club looks ahead to 2027, the aim remains the same: to provide competitive senior cricket, continue growing the women’s game, support junior development and keep the club a welcoming place for players of all ages.
Thank you to everyone who represented, supported and helped Sutton Cricket Club throughout 2026.

articles.title: Remembering Jon Megginson – A Lifetime of Service to Sutton CC
articles.image_alt: Jon Megginson representing Sutton Cricket Club
articles.summary: Sutton Cricket Club remembers Jon Megginson, whose decades of service shaped generations of players and left a lasting legacy across the club.
articles.lead: It is with great sadness that Sutton Cricket Club has learned of the passing of Jon Megginson over the weekend.
body: Jon was a huge part of Sutton Cricket Club for many decades and gave an enormous amount to the club throughout his life.

During his time at Sutton, Jon served in a number of important roles, including Chairman, Captain, Vice President, Colts Coach and Colts Manager. His contribution went far beyond the titles he held, and his influence can still be seen throughout the club today.
Jon was particularly passionate about junior cricket and dedicated countless hours to coaching, encouraging and supporting young players.
Generations of Sutton cricketers benefited from his guidance, and many of the players representing the club today were coached by Jon during their own cricketing journeys.

He played a major part in helping young players develop their confidence and love for the game, while also helping create the welcoming environment that has become such an important part of Sutton Cricket Club.
Jon was also a huge influence in helping establish the club's Ladies team and was always keen to see cricket at Sutton continue to grow and provide opportunities for more people to become involved.
Even up until last season, Jon remained involved as Colts Manager, continuing a lifetime of commitment to supporting the next generation of Sutton cricketers.

For so many people at the club, Jon was much more than a coach or committee member. He was a friend, a familiar face around the ground and someone who genuinely cared about Sutton Cricket Club and the people within it.
His contribution spans decades, teams and generations, and the impact he had on the club will continue long into the future.
Jon's passion for cricket, friendship and unmistakable presence around Sutton CC will be greatly missed by everyone who knew him.
The thoughts and deepest condolences of everyone at Sutton Cricket Club are with Jon's family and friends at this very difficult time.
Thank you for everything, Jon. You will always be part of Sutton Cricket Club.
Rest in peace, Jon. 🏏💛💚

articles.title: Sutton CC Saturday Team of the Year 2026
articles.summary: Our 2026 Saturday Team of the Year, selected from league performances across Sutton's 1st XI and 2nd XI.
articles.lead: After reviewing the 2026 Saturday League season across both the 1st XI and 2nd XI, we have selected a balanced Team of the Year based on consistency, match impact, all-round contribution and the positions players actually filled.
body: 1. Michael Grady – Opener / Bowler. Michael scored 264 1st XI league runs at 33.00, including 127 not out, and took 19 wickets at just 9.47 with best figures of 5/24.
2. Paul Robinson – Opener. Paul scored 263 2nd XI league runs at 43.83, including three half-centuries, and added a further 54 runs for the 1st XI.
3. James Phipps – Top-order batter. James scored 142 league runs for the 2nd XI at 28.40, including two half-centuries, plus another 76 for the 1st XI.

4. James Nuttall – Batter / Bowler. James made 184 runs in only six league innings at 30.67, including a superb 136, and also took eight wickets. His 241-run partnership with Michael Grady against Bluntisham was one of the standout batting performances of the season.
5. James Barrett – Middle-order batter. James scored 156 1st XI league runs, with a highest score of 65 and a strike rate of 104.70.
6. Craig Faux – All-rounder. Craig scored 190 1st XI league runs and took 16 wickets, with best figures of 4/22, while contributing in several important middle and lower-order partnerships.
7. Joshie Pollard – Wicketkeeper / Batter. Joshie scored 114 combined Saturday league runs and recorded four wicketkeeping dismissals across the two Saturday sides.
8. Josh Grady – Bowling all-rounder. Josh was Sutton's leading Saturday league wicket-taker with 22 wickets across the 1st XI and 2nd XI, while also contributing useful lower-order runs.
9. Michael Ward – Bowler. Michael took 13 2nd XI league wickets at an outstanding average of 9.15, including best figures of 5/15.
10. Jack Boston – Bowler. Jack finished with 16 1st XI league wickets, including best figures of 4/9.
11. George Ware – Bowler. George took 12 Saturday league wickets across the two sides, including 10 for the 2nd XI at an economy rate of 3.71.
12th Man: Richard Goodjohn. Richard took nine 1st XI league wickets at 11.56 with an economy rate of 3.47, including a superb 5/17, and was extremely unlucky to miss the final XI.

Honourable mentions go to Daniel Grady, Daniel Abbs, Cornelio Du Plessis, Stephen Tuck, Jordan Emms, Lourens Herselman and Ren Barnard, all of whom made strong contributions during the Saturday league season.
The final XI gives Sutton a realistic batting order, genuine wicketkeeping, several all-round options and a strong bowling attack, while recognising performances from both Saturday sides.

articles.title: Sutton CC celebrates its 2026 award winners
articles.image_alt: Michael Grady receiving a Sutton Cricket Club 2026 award
articles.summary: Sutton Cricket Club celebrates the 2026 award winners across the 1st XI, 2nd XI, Sunday side, club awards and U14s.
articles.lead: Sutton Cricket Club has celebrated its 2026 award winners, recognising performances and contributions across the senior, Sunday, club and junior sections.
body: Michael Grady collected both the 1st XI Batter of the Year and Player of the Year awards, with Josh Grady named 1st XI Bowler of the Year.
For the 2nd XI, James Short was Batter of the Year, Michael Ward Bowler of the Year and Paul Robinson Player of the Year.
Kaiden Grady was named Sunday Player of the Year, Vini Vineeth Fielder of the Year, George Ware Clubman and Josh Pollard Young Player of the Year.
The U14 awards went to Leon Perrin as Batter of the Year, Jason Harnwell as Bowler of the Year and Oscar Pergl-Wilson as Player of the Year.
Congratulations to all of the 2026 winners, and thank you to everyone who contributed to Sutton Cricket Club throughout the season.

articles.title: Colin Coulson Memorial Game raises £275
articles.summary: Paul’s XI beat the Coulson XI by five wickets in a special memorial game that raised £275 for the British Heart Foundation in memory of Colin Coulson.
articles.lead: A huge thank you to everyone who came along and supported the memorial game between the Coulson XI and Paul’s XI. The Coulson XI scored 181/6 before Paul’s XI reached 187/5 to win by five wickets.
body: Batting highlights for the Coulson XI included Lourens Herselman 32*, Phil Coulson 30* and Kaiden Grady 27. For Paul’s XI, Paul Robinson, David Frear and Ricky Paul each made 33*.
The best bowling figures were Jeff Paul 2/17 for Paul’s XI, while Lourens Herselman took 2/27 and Leon Perrin 2/38 for the Coulson XI.
The day was all about coming together to remember Colin and celebrate his life. Thanks to everyone’s incredible generosity, £275 was raised for the British Heart Foundation.
Thank you to all the players, helpers and supporters who made it such a special day in Colin’s memory.

articles.title: Sutton win by seven wickets
articles.summary: James Nuttall and Michael Grady led the chase after Telugu Association were restricted to 80.
articles.lead: Telugu Association were restricted to 80 before Sutton reached 81/3. James Nuttall scored 26 and Michael Grady finished 21 not out.
body: Sutton completed the chase for the loss of three wickets to secure a seven-wicket victory.

articles.title: Grady century powers Sutton to huge victory
articles.summary: Michael Grady hit an unbeaten 127 as Sutton posted 288/3 before dismissing Bluntisham for 87.
articles.lead: Michael Grady hit 127* as Sutton made 288/3. James Nuttall scored 80 and Richard Goodjohn 50*. Bluntisham were dismissed for 87 as Sutton won by 201 runs.
body: It was a dominant Sutton performance, with three major batting contributions setting up a 201-run victory.
